chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ziyad al-Karkhi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man, an old man, who cannot stand up to go to the toilet, and for whom bowing and prostrating is not possible, he said: 'He should nod with his head as a gesture of prostration, and if there is someone for him who raises the head-covering (or the person) to him, let him prostrate; if it is not possible for him to do that, let him nod with his head towards the Qibla as a gesture.' I said: And what about fasting? He said: 'If he is at that limit (of incapacity), Allah has relieved him of it; if he has the means, a charity of a Mudd of food instead of each day is more beloved to me, and if he does not have the capacity for that, there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.الْخُمْرَةَ: Head-covering (or referring to the person's head)
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A Mudd (a specific measure of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for prayer and fasting for an elderly person who cannot stand or prostrate?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter of the 'Involuntary Prayer' (Salat al-Mudtir) details the graduated concessions for the elderly or infirm, prioritizing actual prostration if assisted, then head nodding, and finally eye movement. It extends these physical accommodations to fasting, offering a fidya of one mud of food as a preferred alternative for those with means, while granting full exemption for the destitute. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) in proportion to the individual's capacity.
